title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) in User Profile API
cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
description: An Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) flaw was identified in the RESTful user profile API at /api/v1/users/{id}. A standard authenticated user (UID 1001) can alter the numerical 'id' URL parameter to target another user account (e.g., UID 1042) and retrieve unredacted personally identifiable information (PII), financial account balances, and administrative roles without tenant authorization checks.
technical_impact: Full read and modification capability across all registered user profiles and administrative accounts in the database.
business_impact: Severe regulatory breach under GDPR/CCPA due to unauthorized exposure of executive financial records and identity theft risk.
reproduction_steps: 1. Authenticate to the application as a standard unprivileged user (UID 1001).
2. Intercept the request to retrieve personal profile: GET /api/v1/users/1001.
3. Tamper with the path parameter from '1001' to arbitrary target user '1042'.
4. Send the modified HTTP request with UID 1001's valid session token.
5. Confirm HTTP 200 response returning complete sensitive profile data for user 1042.

evidence.title: Tampered HTTP Request to Target Profile
evidence.description: Sanitized HTTP GET request displaying manipulation of user ID parameter.

evidence.title: Unauthorized User Profile Data Disclosure
evidence.description: Sanitized HTTP 200 response displaying executive profile data leakage.

remediation.tactical: Implement an explicit object-level ownership check verifying that the authenticated session user ID matches the requested resource ID or possesses an active role of 'system_admin'.
remediation.strategic: Adopt indirect resource mapping (UUIDv4 or encrypted references) and enforce policy-based authorization guards (e.g. OPA or middleware decorators) on all data-access layers.
remediation.code_example:
if req.user.id != requested_id and not req.user.has_role('admin'):
    raise ForbiddenException('Unauthorized access to object resource')

title: Publicly Accessible Environment File Exposing Internal Database Credentials
cwe: CWE-552: Files or Directories Accessible to External Parties
description: A backup configuration file (.env.bak) was left in the web server public root directory on lab.graysentinel.internal. Unauthenticated attackers can download this plaintext file to acquire database credentials, JWT HMAC secrets, and infrastructure endpoints.
technical_impact: Direct credential leakage enabling full compromise of the PostgreSQL database cluster and forgeable JWT tokens.
business_impact: Catastrophic infrastructure compromise and persistent unauthorized database access.
reproduction_steps: 1. Issue an unauthenticated HTTP GET request: curl -sI https://lab.graysentinel.internal/.env.bak.
2. Observe HTTP 200 OK response with Content-Type: text/plain.
3. Retrieve full file content to verify plaintext connection strings and tokens.

evidence.title: Leaked Environment Configuration Dump
evidence.description: Sanitized dump of the .env.bak file showing database and JWT parameters.

remediation.tactical: Delete .env.bak from the production server webroot immediately and rotate all database passwords and JWT secrets.
remediation.strategic: Configure web server block rules to deny all access to dot-files and backup extensions (.bak, .old, .tmp), and store secrets in a managed vault.

title: Absence of Defensive HTTP Security Headers
description: The web server fails to emit modern defense-in-depth HTTP security headers including Content-Security-Policy (CSP), Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS), and X-Frame-Options. This deficiency increases the application's susceptibility to clickjacking and script injection.
technical_impact: Enables clickjacking in transparent iframes and permits mixed-content downgrade attacks in modern web browsers.
business_impact: Increases phishing susceptibility and fails automated compliance security audits.
reproduction_steps: 2. Observe that zero matching security headers are returned in the response headers.

evidence.title: Missing Headers Reconnaissance Dump
evidence.description: Header inspection dump confirming absent security directives.

remediation.tactical: Add HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, and X-Content-Type-Options to the Nginx ingress server configuration.
remediation.strategic: Implement automated CI/CD header compliance validation tests and enforce strict CSP policies.
